description.narrative:
Projektet "Strengthening Science-Policy Interface and Universities’ Research Capacities for Forest Landscape Governance in Southeast Asia: Explore Phase 2" ligger i linje med Strategi för Sveriges regionala utvecklingssamarbete med Asien och Oceanien 2022-2026 och Strategi för Sveriges utvecklingssamarbete inom forskning för fattigdomsbekämpning och hållbar utveckling 2022-2026. Projektet genomförs på lokal, nationell och regional nivå, med särskilt fokus på universitet och forskare i Kambodja, Indonesien, Laos, Myanmar, Filippinerna, Thailand, Timor Lesté och Vietnam.
Projektet bidrar till följande specifika prioriteringar i Strategin för forskningssamarbete och forskning i utveckling:
- Stärkt forskningskapacitet och hållbara forskningsmiljöer. Projektet kommer att stärka forskningskapaciteten vid universitet i åtta länder genom forskningsbidrag, nätverksmöten, seminarier, jämställdhetsprojekt inom universitet, och vetenskapligt mentorskap.
- Stärkt global, regional och nationell forskning av relevans för minst utvecklade länder och regioner. Projektet kommer att leda till mer regional forskning om relationen mellan skogsbruk och jämställdhet, klimatförändringar, miljö, biodiversitet, mänskliga rättigheter, fattigdomsbekämpning och återhämtning från covid-19 pandemin.
- Stärkt genomslag för forskning av relevans för fattigdomsbekämpning och hållbar utveckling. Projektets fokus på deltagarinriktad och insatsbaserad forksning kommer att öka forskarnas förmåga att samarbeta och samverka med beslutsfattare, utvecklingsaktörer, skogsbrukare och samhällsmedlemmar. Detta kommer att leda till en samproducerad kunskapsproduktion som har långsiktiga positiva effekter för marginaliserade och utsatta grupper.
Projektet kompletterar Sveriges strategi för regionala utvecklingssamarbeten i Asien och Oceanien genom att bidra till hållbar utveckling i skogsområden i Sydostasien. Projektets metod integrerar mänskliga rättigheter och jämställdhet samt inkluderar marginaliserade grupper och grupper som lever i fattigdom. Svenskt stöd till projektet kommer att resultera i nya aktörer (sekretariatet, nätverket och forskningsgrupperna) som kan arbeta regionalt i Sydostasien för att hantera nationella och gränsöverskridande utmaningar relaterade till skog, skogsbruk, och skogsförvaltning. Projektet samarbetar också med befintliga institutioner och organisationer som universitet, organisationer i civilsamhället, myndigheter och ASEAN. Initiativets föreslagna arbetsmetod motsvarar Sveriges egen prioritering av integrerade strategier vilka underlättar kommunikation och samarbete mellan civilsamhället, myndigheter, privata företag och forskning. Samtidigt stödjer projektet dessa aktörers förmåga att bidra till utvecklingen av oberoende arenor för informationsspridning, nätverkande och ansvarsutkrävande i relation till mänskliga rättigheter och främjandet av en miljömässigt hållbar utveckling i Sydostasen.

The project "Strengthening Science-Policy Interface and Universities’ Research Capacities for Forest Landscape Governance in Southeast Asia: Explore Phase 2" is aligned with the Strategy for Sweden’s Regional Development Cooperation with Asia and Oceania 2022-2026, and the Strategy for Sweden’s Development Cooperation within Research for Poverty Elimination and Sustainable Development 2022-2026. The project is carried out local, national and regional levels, with special focus on universities and researchers in Cambodia, Indonesia, Laos, Myanmar, the Philippines, Thailand, Timor Lesté and Vietnam.
The project contributes to the following priorities of the Strategy for Sweden’s Development Cooperation within Research for Poverty Elimination and Sustainable Development 2022-2026:
- Strengthened research capacity and sustainable research environments. The project will strengthen research capacity at universities in eight countries through research grants, network meetings, seminars, gender-equality projects within universities, and mentorship.
Strengthened global, regional and national research of relevance for least developed countries and regions. The project will lead to more regional research on the relationship between forest landscape resources and gender equality, climate change, environment, biodiversity, human rights, poverty elimination, and recovery from the covid-19 pandemic.
- Strengthened impact of research that is relevant for poverty elimination and sustainable development. The project's focus on participatory action research will increase researchers' capacity to cooperate and coordinate with decision makers, development actors, forest-users and community members. This will lead to new knowledge with long-term positive impacts for marginalized and vulnerable groups.
The project contributes to the Strategy for Sweden’s Regional Development Cooperation with Asia and Oceania 2022-2026 by contributing to sustainable development in forest landscapes of Southeast Asia. The project's approach integrates human rights and gender equality, and it includes marginalized groups and groups that live in poverty. Sweden's support will result in new actors (e.g. the Explore Secretariat, Explore Network, and transboundary research groups) that can work regionally to address national and transboundary problems related to forests, forest management, and forest use. The project cooperates with already existing institutions and organizations including universities, civil society organizations, government agencies, and ASEAN. The project uses a multistakeholder approach that encourages stakeholders to contribute to free and independent exchange of knowledge, networking, and respect for human rights and environmentally sustainable development in Southeast Asia.

The overall objective of Explore is to support governments in using high quality research to improve policies and institutional frameworks for the inclusive and sustainable management of forest landscapes in Southeast Asia that contributes to the climate and development goals such as SDGs.
Phase 2 of Explore will lead to innovative and well designed and implemented research that is widely used by key stakeholders, including to support informed policy and decision making at landscape, national and regional levels. The specific objectives of the initiative are:
- Regional, transboundary research projects are using participatory methods to develop and conduct high quality research on forest landscape governance in Southeast Asia
- Researchers are supporting informed policy making and implementation across the region
-Researchers of forest landscape governance in Southeast Asia have a stronger network with policy and decision makers at landscape, national, regional and international levels
- A member driven and inclusive forest landscape governance research network is fully functional
- The communication and knowledge strategy fosters visibility, awareness, engagement, access to knowledge assets and uptake of research findings
-Strategic universities and research institutions in the region have a clear program in place and access to resources to support female researchers of forest landscape governance and to strengthen the quality of research of gender issues related to forest landscape governance

Year 1 - The Explore Forest Landscape Governance Research Network has increased in membership from 293 people at the end of Phase 1 to 520 members as of 30 September 2023.
- During the first year of Explore 2, seven research projects received funding. Each project has a 3 or 4 year duration, and is expected to reach completion between April 2026 - April 2027. Total funding released to the projects during year 1 was USD 257 717. Teams included a total of 119 researchers (62 women and 57 men).
Year 2 Explore has seen a rapid and robust progress during year 2 and is now supported by a full team within the Explore Secretariat. The focus in the second year has been on advancing the technical components of the project building on the administrative and management focus in the first year. The dialog with the Embassy on, and subsequent approval of, annual work plans and budgets has enabled Explore to address co-funding gaps for research teams and strategically focus on research support, network development and linking research to policy.
Overall, Explore has successfully launched almost all major programme activities originally proposed and planned by the end of the second year. One activity still remains, i.e., research institutional grant, which will be launched in Q4 in the third year. Throughout the year, ongoing activities, such as research grants, capacity development, communications, network development, and elements of programme management have been strengthened significantly to sharpen the focus on research projects, enhance the Secretariats support to researchers, and expand the reach and programmes engagement with stakeholders. The Embassy noted that the annual report for 23/24 could focus more on outcomes and changes and this will be followed up the coming years to track improvement in reporting.
During year 2, Explore has for example:
1. Full scale, smooth and on track research implementation, illustrated by steady progress across various stages of research in line with the research plans of the seven grantees. The entire budget has been endorsed to support high-quality research results. Key activities undertaken this year include data collection and analysis, the sharing of initial research findings through journal publications and presentations in international conferences and policy outreach efforts.
2. Targeted technical support for the seven research teams through grants monitoring visits (in preparation, during, and follow-ups), enabled proactive and two-way communication between the Secretariat and the research teams. Barriers to research implementation (e.g., government approval, mentor, research approaches) were raised openly, and addressed promptly, leading to resolutions in a responsive and collaborative manner.
3. Improved capacities in research communication and project management for researchers. Communication strategies and stakeholder engagement plan of actions were developed during the end of the regional training and subsequently followed up at country level in the national training. Participants highly valued these learning opportunities, as such topics are not commonly and readily available to researchers in the region.
4. A strategic policy outreach and coordination plan has been developed as a road map to guide researchers in influencing policymakers. This involves working closely with national research teams to incorporate landscape and national-level policies, capacity development on policy outreach and establishing and facilitating National Advisory Committees (NAC) in respective countries.
5. NACs have been formed in Indonesia and Viet Nam, with members from multiple sectors (e.g. government, private sector, academia, NGOs) to provide guidance to Explore and research teams in specific country contexts. Following the establishment of the committees, NAC meetings will be held and committee members will be involved in in-country activities, enhancing Explores efforts to influence policy and decision-making at the landscape, national and regional levels. NACs in other countries are in the process of nomination and formation.
6. An adaptive and reinforced approach to creating a member-driven Explore Community of Practice has been established, with the founding and core members (through setting of rules and mechanisms by founding and core members PIs and co-PIs of the seven research teams) setting rules and mechanisms. The virtual community, hosted by the Global Landscapes Forum (GLF), grew to 1,027 members (up from 520 in Sep 2023) will transition from GLF to the Transformative Partnership Platform on Agroecology in Sep 2024. An offline research network on forest landscape government is concurrently being fostered and facilitated.
7. Collaborative efforts between RECOFTC and CIFOR-ICRAF have expanded in Year 2 advancing a range of programme activities. The announcement of the women PhD scholarships on both organizations websites and social media platforms successfully profiled Explore. CIFOR-ICRAFs contribution to the regional and national training sessions, has diversified approach (panel discussion), added valuable contents (popular research writing), and adapted training into relevant contexts (Indonesia-based research).
8. Two women PhD research scholars were selected through a competitive process as set out in the grant selection and administration guidelines developed in Year 1. The scholarship, awarded for two and a half years, will support research on forest landscapes in Explores priority countries Cambodia, Lao People's Democratic Republic, Myanmar and Timor-Leste.
